title: The converse binomial inequality for alpha>2
statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb N$, $\alpha>2$, and $x,y\geq 0$. **Converse binomial inequality.** One has

$$
2^{\alpha-1}\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{\alpha k}{\alpha j}x^{\alpha j}y^{\alpha(k-j)}\geq (x+y)^{\alpha k}.
$$

This is proposed as an appropriate inequality comparing the generalized binomial sum with $(x+y)^{\alpha k}$ in the range $\alpha>2$, where the preceding lower bound without the factor $2^{\alpha-1}$ is stated not to hold. The source leaves this statement for future research and provides no resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.02747

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).
source_name: Stefan Gerhold and Thomas Simon, “A converse to the neo-classical inequality with an application to the Mittag-Leffler function”, arXiv:2111.02747 (2021).
